facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of a slowly growing, dull, intermittent swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule
fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area
teeth #15 and #16 were grossly carious
a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa
no tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth
a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices
a provisional diagnosis of a periapical abscess was made
Preoperative blood tests (CBC, hemoglobin, blood sugar, bleeding and clotting times) were within normal limits
curettage yielded a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue
a provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma

concepts.why: The patient presented with a slowly growing swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, with fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area, which is consistent with a periapical abscess.
The curettage yielded a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue, which is consistent with a periapical granuloma.
The patient had grossly carious teeth, which is consistent with dental caries.

The patient had a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa and a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices, which is consistent with chronic periapical periodontitis.

The patient presented with a slowly growing swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, with fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area, which is consistent with acute periapical periodontitis.
The patient had a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices and a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue was yielded during curettage, which is consistent with a periapical cyst.
The patient had a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa, which is consistent with gingivitis.
The patient had a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa and a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices, which is consistent with periodontitis.
